newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian mayor's fascist name plans split council.
newsitem.headline: Italian mayor's fascist name plans split council.

text.p: A battle is brewing in the town of Latina south of Rome over a plan by its mayor to give Fascist-era names to some of its streets, Italian newspapers reported on Wednesday.
They said the proposal by mayor Ajmone Finestra, 75, of the hard right National Alliance party, had split the council, with opponents demanding that the idea be put to a referendum.
"This sounds more like a declaration of war than a plan to keep historical memories alive," the Rome newspaper Il Messaggero quoted Greens party councillor Luigi Di Mambro as saying.
Latina was built under dictator Benito Mussolini's Fascist rule on land reclaimed in the 1920s by draining the malaria-infested Pontine Marshes south of Rome.
Finestra, who fought for Mussolini in World War Two, was not available for comment but his office confirmed that he wanted to name the town centre district Littoria.
The town's main park, nameless for decades, was named the "Arnaldo Mussolini Park" after the Duce's brother a year ago.
